bib.title: Large Scale GAN Training for High Fidelity Natural Image Synthesis

read.skipped: References skimmed; Appendix A and F figures are images with no extractable content.

question: Can class-conditional GANs trained at much larger scale produce high-resolution, diverse ImageNet samples, and what limits their stability?
hypothesis: Scaling batch size and width, plus orthogonal regularisation and a truncation trick, closes the fidelity and variety gap between GANs and real images.
contributions: Scale GANs to 2-4x the parameters and 8x the batch size of prior art, with shared embeddings and skip-z
Truncation trick for fidelity/variety control, enabled by orthogonal regularisation
Characterise instabilities of large-scale GANs via singular values of G and D

method.summary: SA-GAN-based class-conditional ResNet GANs (BigGAN, BigGAN-deep) trained on ImageNet at 128, 256, 512 px and on a JFT-300M subset with batch 2048 on TPU v3 pods. Hinge loss, spectral norm, shared class embedding, hierarchical z, off-diagonal orthogonal regularisation, EMA of G weights.

datasets.name: ImageNet ILSVRC 2012
datasets.split: training set for training; train and validation IS reported
datasets.preprocessing: crop along long edge, rescale with area resampling

datasets.name: JFT-300M subset
datasets.preprocessing: single label sampled randomly each time an image is sampled

models.name: BigGAN
models.params: G 70.4M and D 88.0M at 128x128; 158.3M total in Table 1 row 8
models.architecture: ResNet GAN, one non-local block, shared embedding, chunked skip-z (20-D chunks)

models.name: BigGAN-deep
models.architecture: bottleneck ResBlocks, 2 blocks per resolution, four times deeper than BigGAN, attention at 64x64

training.objective: hinge-loss GAN; class conditioning by conditional BatchNorm in G and projection in D
training.lr: BigGAN: 2e-4 D, 5e-5 G at all resolutions; BigGAN-deep 128px same, 256/512px 2.5e-5 both
training.steps: stable runs to 1e6 iterations in Table 1; models collapse earlier (e.g. 152 to 371 thousand)
training.precision: inferred: low precision on TPU (epsilon raised from 1e-8 to 1e-4 in BatchNorm and Spectral Norm to mollify low-precision numerical issues)
training.regularisation: orthogonal regularisation beta=1e-4 on G (off-diagonal form); spectral norm in G and D; 2 D steps per G step; EMA of G decay 0.9999
training.hardware: Google TPU v3 Pod, 128/256/512 cores for 128/256/512 px
training.seeds: Table 1 rows other than 1-4: 8 random initialisations; Table 2: at least three

other.cross_replica_BN: batch stats aggregated across all devices

inference.decoding: sampling z from truncated normal, threshold swept (sigma 0 to 2)

parameters.truncation_threshold: 0.5 for Fig 4 samples; swept for Table 2

metrics.name: FID
metrics.definition: Frechet Inception Distance, Heusel et al. 2017

eval.protocol: Table 2 reports no-truncation, best-FID, FID at validation-data IS, and FID at max IS; JFT uses an Inception v2 trained on JFT.

availability.code: Pretrained generators on TF Hub (tfhub.dev/s?q=biggan); training code not stated

results.claim: BigGAN-deep at 128x128 on ImageNet reaches IS 166.5 and FID 7.4, against SA-GAN 52.52 and 18.65.
results.setup: ImageNet ILSVRC 2012, 128x128, BigGAN-deep; scores taken at the truncation setting where the model's IS equals that of real validation data (Table 2 column 5), not untruncated.
results.note: Abstract and Sec 1 print 166.5 and 7.4 without stating the truncation setting. Untruncated BigGAN-deep 128 is FID 5.7, IS 124.5 (column 3); best-FID truncation is 6.3/148.1.
results.table: Table 2, row BigGAN-deep 128, column FID / (valid IS): 7.4 ± .6/166.5 ± 1; row SA-GAN 128: 18.65/52.52

results.claim: Best FID at 128x128 is 5.7 untruncated for BigGAN-deep.
results.setup: ImageNet 128x128, BigGAN-deep, no truncation, at least three random initialisations.

results.claim: At 256x256 the paper reports IS 232.5 and FID 8.1; at 512x512 IS 241.5 and FID 11.5.
